authors: M. Gehrig, H. Lentz, E. U. Franck
title: The System Water - Carbon Dioxide - Sodium Chloride to 773 K and 300 MPa
experimental_method: Synthetic method in a variable-volume autoclave with sapphire window: known amounts of NaCl solution (weighed, known concentration) and CO2 (weighed storage cylinder) filled at room temperature; temperature raised at constant piston position and the p-T curve recorded; the break point of the isochoric p-T curve (two-phase to one-phase transition), usually confirmed visually, gives a point on the phase boundary surface (isopleth) together with the molar volume.
uncertainties_stated: Pressure better than 0.2 MPa; temperature 0.5 K near 373 K rising to 2 K at 773 K; sample composition 0.2 mol%; molar volume about 0.4% (within 1% at higher T and P below 15 MPa); phase separation temperatures at and above 673 K up to +-5 K in the critical ranges.
quality_remarks: Composition is the overall filling composition, not an analysed phase composition. Sub-table 20 composition sums to 99.80 mol% (14.61 + 0.29 + 84.90) as printed. Several sub-tables list rows out of monotonic order (kept as printed). 'Weight% relative to water' in the title is numerically consistent with mass fraction of NaCl in the CO2-free salt solution (6 g NaCl per 100 g solution), not g NaCl per 100 g water. Authors report agreement with Takenouchi and Kennedy near 6.7 mol% CO2, and a later repeat of the 4 mol% isopleth by Uematsu confirmed the results.
